static_traits.name: Diana
static_traits.educational_background: Attending a private high school and taking college-credit courses
static_traits.family_status: Both parents have heavy European accents
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends, but reduced socializing due to the scholarship application and worries, tending toward self-isolation
static_traits.medical_history: No similar history of psychological problems; not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, logic fairly good, tone rather negative; catastrophizing predictions and overgeneralization exist; skeptical about suggestions but can consider small-step attempts, cooperativeness acceptable

basic_info.main_problem: I believe that since my parents pay high tuition for private high school, I will not receive a college scholarship.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling when these thoughts began to affect my motivation to apply for scholarships and plan for college.

core_beliefs: It is impossible for me to receive a college scholarship

special_situations.event: When researching university options and financial-aid information, noticed that private high school tuition is very high
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my parents have already paid high tuition for my private high school, then I will not be eligible for a college scholarship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces or delays scholarship applications, worries excessively and repeatedly looks up information to try to gain certainty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will not be eligible for a scholarship

special_situations.event: When starting to seriously plan college and scholarship applications
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot be guaranteed a scholarship, then investing in planning and applying is meaningless
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: With no guarantee, do not waste time

special_situations.event: When friends think I am 'overreacting' to the scholarship issue and find it hard to understand my worries
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not agree with or do not understand my anxiety, I must distance myself from them and bear the pressure alone
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids communicating with friends, socially isolated, putting all energy into applications
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not understand me; I can only carry it myself

special_situations.event: Situations of worrying that the schedule will be disrupted by sudden tasks, thus falling behind the application progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once any interruption occurs, I will miss the opportunity and fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Skeptical of new strategies, avoids trying, and continues over-managing and worrying
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If the plan is disrupted, I will fail

core_conflict.wish: Longs for stable support and recognition (achieving acceptance and funding through the scholarship)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected, unable to afford college, thus with limited prospects
defense_goal: Reducing the pain of being rejected by lowering expectations and avoiding applying
Maintaining a sense of control by excessively focusing on uncertainty

object_relations.self_representation: A lonely and highly stressed applicant, with decreased drive, needing to carry it alone
object_relations.object_representation: Others (like friends) who do not understand one's pressure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes trying a new time arrangement or behavioral experiment to balance applications and socializing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting 'no guarantee' as 'not feasible', avoiding trying in a rationalized way (transference: equating uncertainty with failure)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone of caution and doubt, emphasizing uncertainty and lack of guarantee, postponing or negating attempts with logical reasons

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing talking with friends about academic and financial worries or obtaining support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will not understand or will only negate oneself, thus turning the urge to seek support into pressuring oneself (transference: expecting to be ignored)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoids asking for support, emphasizes 'I will bear it myself', reduces emotional expression, and instead doubles down on doing application tasks alone

manifestations: Reducing time with friends to focus on the scholarship application, avoiding talking about academics and financial worries, feeling 'really lonely'
When facing uncertainty, hoping for a 'guarantee'; feeling anxious about choosing and taking responsibility for oneself, worrying about missing opportunities
outcomes: Excessive control and planning disrupting daily routines

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt and worrying about missing opportunities
Insists on guarantees before daring to try
Highly cautious and skeptical about time-scheduling strategies

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Avoiding discussing academic and financial worries with friends
Turning the need to seek support into self-pressure and completing the application alone

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Avoiding directly trying new behavioral strategies on the grounds of 'no guarantee'
Avoiding facing the current application actions through generalization and predicting the future

positive_force: Good academic performance, with a certain level of learning and self-management ability
Has a few friends they can reach out to
negative_force: Catastrophic prediction and jumping to conclusions (predicting the future)
Overgeneralization leading to self-doubt and decreased drive
Excessive worry about college finances, routines disrupted

target_behavior.behavior: Excessively worries about college finances and scholarships; repeatedly looks up information
antecedent: Researching university options and financial-aid information
When starting to consider college and scholarships
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic prediction and overgeneralization about 'being unable to receive a scholarship'
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain certainty and a sense of control, to alleviate the anxiety brought by uncertainty

antecedent: When preparing or submitting scholarship application materials
When facing the application process and deadlines
target_behavior.core_reason: Self-doubt and fear of being rejected (driven by overgeneralization and predicting the future)
target_behavior.function: Escaping the pain of failure and rejection
target_behavior.consequence: Application progress blocked, may miss the opportunity

target_behavior.behavior: Social isolation, less time with friends
antecedent: When friends question the worry or think the reaction is excessive
When needing to discuss academic and financial issues with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Believing others do not understand oneself; turning to bearing it alone after failing to seek external validation
target_behavior.function: Escapes evaluation and conflict, maintains a fragile sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Increased sense of loneliness, reduced social support, stress and anxiety worsened
